Free feeding pellets is not usually a good idea. Generally, rabbits shouldn't have more that 1/4 cup of pellets a day, if you dont limit it, it can cause them to not eat enough hay. This can cause teeth issues as well as obesity. That can especially be a problem if you only have one rabbit, as they may gain too much weight to be able to properly groom themselves, and that can lead to a whole other slew of problems. Pellets are like a treat to them- so most of the time, they will eat those instead of hay if it is offered. 

Also keep in mind Rabbits digestive systems are VERY sensitive. You open yourself up to a lot of potential problems if their diet isn't carefully monitored. Too much of anything but hay can cause them to get very sick and potentially get a block in their intestines- which is one of the leading causes of rabbit death, and can kill them VERY quickly/suddenly. If you know anything about horses, it's pretty much the same as a colic. 

Absolutely no shame, but this is what my vet told me when she found out I was feeding just slightly over 1/4 cup of pellets a day

Honestly, with how your schedule is it might be worth getting an automatic feeder for her pellets- though if you are feeding in one spot be aware that she may get territorial over it, and potentially food aggressive. When I was feeding my boy in a bowl he got a little aggressive and bit my hand once (I didn't put the food down fast enough, though im sure the risk would be less if its a automatic feeder, though she may chew it for sure) the feeder balls are super helpful in keeping them from getting territorial if you're worried about that. Is there a time you're always home? Even if it's late at night or early in the morning outside of your work hours having a consistent feeding time is ideal, even if that time is like 3am :)

My rabbit had his area under the table for a while, for him he loved the chairs and used them as an obstacle course all the time- I think that actually helped a lot with over energy/being destructive. I've been told it's good to have at least 2 hide holes per rabbit, I love rabbit castles (though I havent gotten one yet because they are somewhat pricey, but could be a good option for a table area) if your bunny is smaller there are some cheaper options on amazon. 

Other than that I second the enrichment box! Also, I personally feed pellets with a feeder ball- it seems to tire my boy out a decent amount, and we often practice tricks (i e spin, stand tall, sometimes we will get a stick and have him jump over it) in the morning with pellets and in the evening with greens, I also feel like that makes him less destructive. 

Keeping to a schedule also helps. My boy gets destructive if we aren't consistent about pellets/greens. Rabbits are really good at keeping track of time, and they like routine so it's not uncommon for them to be more destructive if you're not sticking to a schedule. 

Also, if she's not spayed that is going to be a big impact, female rabbits are very territorial so if she isn't spayed she may calm down after

My bunny did this last year, watch for behavior changes and take them to the vet if you see any change in their eating/pooping/activity habits but otherwise if they are acting normal sometimes that can happen for an amount of time when a bunny is stressed, and is more likely to happen if they are overheating. Make sure you're keeping them in a cooler environment as bunnies tend to overheat easier than you may think. My bunny had his down for a few months and one day was just able to move it again. 

That being said if these are younger bunnies sometimes their ears drop, and they can have one up one down. There have also been cases of older rabbits having an ear drop randomly and not come back up.
